implemented_requirements.requirement: Computer selects a hidden sequence of colors (or digits)
implemented_requirements.evidence: secret_code.py defines class SecretCode which generates a random code using the provided palette and length, respecting the allow_duplicates flag.

implemented_requirements.requirement: Player attempts to guess within a set number of tries
implemented_requirements.evidence: MastermindGame.play (game.py) loops while len(self.history) < self.max_attempts, prompting the player for input each iteration.

implemented_requirements.requirement: After each guess, show feedback regarding correct color and correct position
implemented_requirements.evidence: calculate_feedback (feedback.py) returns exact and partial match counts; history.render (history.py) displays these via render_pegs (ui.py) after each guess.

implemented_requirements.requirement: Distinguish between exact matches and partial color matches
implemented_requirements.evidence: Feedback dataclass stores exact_matches and partial_matches separately; render_pegs uses different symbols (EXACT_PEG and PARTIAL_PEG) for each.
MastermindGame.play prints a win message when feedback.is_win is true, otherwise prints a lose message after attempts are exhausted or an abort message on quit.

critical_issues: Two duplicate modules (gamehistory.py and mastermindgame.py, plus secretcode.py) exist but are not imported; they do not affect execution but add unnecessary noise.
history.render uses a placeholder "..." in the unused gamehistory.py version, but the imported history.py implementation is complete.
judge.summary: The repository contains a complete, runnable implementation of the classic Mastermind game. Core mechanics—secret code generation, guess input, duplicate‑safe feedback, exact vs. partial peg distinction, attempt limits, and win/lose messaging—are all present and wired together. Minor code duplication does not impede functionality, so the solution meets the benchmark requirements.
